facts.fact: TechAfrica News states that SmartCare Pro, Zambia's electronic health records platform, is already deployed in more than 2,000 health facilities nationwide; the count is of health facilities of every kind, with no denominator and no split for primary clinics; undated, so the publication date is used.

GovLink Private 4G was launched at Ndola Teaching Hospital, reported 16 July 2026, with SmartCare Pro and Care 2.0 among the first systems to move onto the government-owned network; the Ministry of Health's permanent secretary said inadequate digital infrastructure had limited the electronic health systems until then.
Care 2.0 is being piloted at Ndola Teaching Hospital, Arthur Davison Children's Hospital and Kitwe Teaching Hospital, per TechAfrica News on 16 July 2026.
Care 2.0 is at pilot stage in three Copperbelt hospitals (Ndola Teaching, Arthur Davison Children's, Kitwe Teaching) as of 16 July 2026; the document names no primary clinic using it.

systems.tiers: pilot at Ndola Teaching Hospital, Arthur Davison Children's Hospital and Kitwe Teaching Hospital

systems.owner: e-Government Division, SMART Zambia Institute, with IHM Southern Africa, Tuso Business Dynamics, Quadrupleplay and the Ministry of Health
